o: Compare searching methods with correct prerequisites.
Choose and trace a suitable sorting algorithm.
Answer multi-step OCR-style searching and sorting questions.
c: Linear search inspects elements sequentially and works with unsorted lists. Binary search can discard halves but needs sorted input.
When explaining an algorithm, show the actual array values, tested positions and changes—not merely the algorithm's name.
Bubble compares and swaps adjacent pairs; insertion places a key into a sorted portion; merge divides and combines sorted lists.
A question about one pass is not a request for complete sorting. A question about a search index uses zero-based array positions.

m.title: Model Searching and Sorting Exam Practice
m.q: A club has an unsorted list [5,2,9,1]. Explain which search method can be used immediately and trace the search for 9. [4 marks]
st: Because the list is unsorted, choose linear search [1].
Compare first item 5, not a match [1].
Compare second item 2, not a match [1].
Third item 9 matches, so return zero-based index 2 [1].

w: A sorted array is [2,4,6,8,10]. Trace binary search for 8. [4 marks]
First mid index 2 = 6 [1]. Target 8 is larger [1], so search right indices 3–4 [1]. Mid = 3 value 8 found at index 3 [1].
A pupil sorts [4,1,3] using bubble sort. Show the first complete pass. [3 marks]
Compare 4 and 1 [1], swap to [1,4,3] [1]; compare 4 and 3, swap to [1,3,4] [1].
Explain why binary search should not be applied directly to [8,1,4,6] and how to prepare it. [3 marks]
Array is unsorted [1]. Binary search discards halves based on order [1]. Sort ascending [1,4,6,8] before applying it [1].
wSteps: Check that the array is sorted.
Without order a discarded half may contain target.
Sort the values into ascending order.
Binary search can now operate safely.

k.q: Trace linear search over a sorted list then explain whether binary search is also possible.
k.code:
array values = [1,3,5,7,9]
found = -1
for i=0 to 4
    if values[i] == 7 AND found == -1 then
        found = i
    endif
next i
print(found)
p: Explain the sorted-array requirement for binary search.
k.a: Target 7 is at index 3. Target 9 is at index 4. Binary search could also be used because [1,3,5,7,9] is sorted.
